pre1986_automatic_lexical_literature_bri.candidate: Could fish-oil supplementation affect Raynaud symptoms through a change in blood viscosity?
not_entailed_reasons: Vascular-disease treatment data are not automatically transportable to Raynaud primary or secondary cohorts
Association of Raynaud with viscosity is not causal proof
Pre-1986 primary-Raynaud null study and venesection intervention challenge a simplistic mediator
Trial and prior-art novelty were not established using the early source subset alone

pre1986_automatic_pattern_extractions.source_author: Tietjen GW, Chien S, Leroy EC, Gavras I, Gavras H, Gump FE.

source_provenance.exact_evidence: mean plasma viscosity was significantly (P less than .01) elevated over established normal controls

known_limits: Study primarily involves secondary disease, not primary
Association does not prove viscosity causes disease

source_provenance.exact_evidence: viscosity of the patients' blood was significantly higher (p less than 0.05) at 27 degrees C than that of the controls when measured at a low shear-rate

pre1986_automatic_pattern_extractions.source_author: Jahnsen T, Nielsen SL, Skovborg F.

source_provenance.exact_evidence: no significant difference, however, in whole-blood and plasma viscosity between ten young women with primary Raynaud's phenomenon and ten age and sex matched controls

known_limits: Failure to find a difference is not proof all primary Raynaud has normal viscosity
Sample ten patients and ten controls

additional_intervention_negative.exact_evidence: Venesection, which reduces plasma viscosity, did not change the ease with which Raynaud's phenomenon was provoked in five patients

pre1986_automatic_pattern_extractions.source_author: Blunt RJ, George AJ, Hurlow RA, Strachan CJ, Stuart J.

source_provenance.exact_evidence: Whole-blood viscosity (measured at 128, 23 and 0.2 s-(1) was significantly increased in 29 females with Raynaud's syndrome

known_limits: Disease mechanism may not be single-factor viscosity

pre1986_automatic_pattern_extractions.source_author: Woodcock BE, Smith E, Lambert WH, Jones WM, Galloway JH, Greaves M, Preston FE.

source_provenance.exact_evidence: A statistically significant reduction in whole blood viscosity was observed at seven weeks

known_limits: Independent PAD group, not Raynaud patients
No transfer to clinical disease outcome without an additional causal premise

independent_followup_randomized_study.trial_authors: DiGiacomo RA, Kremer JM, Shah DM.
independent_followup_randomized_study.design_text: Thirty-two patients with primary or secondary Raynaud's phenomenon were randomly assigned
independent_followup_randomized_study.treatment: fish oil vs olive oil placebo; subgroup primary versus secondary

reported_numbers_source.text: increased from 31.3 +/- 1.3 minutes baseline to 46.5 +/- 2.1 minutes at six weeks (p = 0.04)

independent_followup_randomized_study.reported_subgroup_result: benefit in primary, not established in secondary

subgroup_conclusion_source.exact_evidence: conclude that the ingestion of fish oil improves tolerance to cold exposure and delays the onset of vasospasm in patients with primary, but not secondary, Raynaud's phenomenon

critical_limitations: Small n=32 full trial, subgroup numbers small; no patient-level data to independently recompute p values
Primary and secondary effects cannot be silently pooled as identical
Original trial did not prove effect mediated only by whole-blood viscosity
Published plus-minus statistics have no provided covariance; cannot compute paired uncertainty from aggregate text alone

limitations: Curated small set of actual papers and narrow hand-specified text patterns; the system did NOT discover all relevant PubMed articles by itself
A lexical shared-concept join produces a candidate question, not logically valid causal inference or demonstrated novel discovery
Author identity and study group are read from metadata and bounded source spans, not model-extracted DRS
An original 1986 abstract is unavailable; no pretending its title is full original text
The later RCT interpretation relies on reported paper authors and text; there was no independent clinical replication or patient-level reanalysis
Other Raynaud studies were not exhaustively retrieved and current treatment recommendations are outside this historical discovery check
Some original 1975/1976/1977 differences are scope, cohort and measurement condition differences, not strict logical contradiction
